root_cause.text: Integer overflow in `xdr_round_up(ticket_len)` when `ticket_len` is near the maximum value, allowing an incorrect length check that could lead to out-of-bounds access.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes the condition from `xdr_round_up(ticket_len) > token_len - sizeof(container)` to `ticket_len > xdr_round_down(token_len - sizeof(container))`. The commit message states: "Fix potential integer overflow in rxgk_extract_token() when checking the length of the ticket. Rather than rounding up the value to be tested (which might overflow), round down the size of the available data." This confirms the overflow occurs when rounding up `ticket_len`, and the fix avoids it by instead rounding down the safe capacity.

Author: David Howells <dhowells@redhat.com>

    rxrpc: Fix untrusted unsigned subtract
    
    Fix the following Smatch static checker warning:
    
       net/rxrpc/rxgk_app.c:65 rxgk_yfs_decode_ticket()
       warn: untrusted unsigned subtract. 'ticket_len - 10 * 4'
    
    by prechecking the length of what we're trying to extract in two places in

bic_trace_step.reason: The diff adds early length checks in both rxgk_yfs_decode_ticket and rxgk_extract_token, preventing unsigned subtraction underflow. In rxgk_yfs_decode_ticket, a check for ticket_len < 10*sizeof(__be32) is inserted before any subtraction. In rxgk_extract_token, a check for token_len < sizeof(container) is added and the subtraction token_len - sizeof(container) is now guarded (the prior code had token_len - 3*4 without such a guard). Thus the vulnerable construct (untrusted unsigned subtract) is no longer present in the code after this commit.
